answer.rationale: The competitor's price cut creates immediate churn pressure on price-sensitive SMB accounts. However, memory_73 and exp_73 show that targeted promotional pricing is a retention trap—it acquired cohorts with -12% 30-day retention and did not survive first renewal. Competing on price directly would worsen long-term qualified revenue. Instead, activate the proven levers from memory_86 (onboarding shortening) and memory_91 (activation messaging) to deepen product engagement and time-to-value for at-risk accounts. Engaged customers show higher renewal intent independent of price. This addresses the immediate churn risk while preserving the cohort quality and renewal economics that define sustainable growth. memory_31 (signup simplification) is held in reserve if early activation messaging shows insufficient lift. Referral incentives and enterprise sales assist are lower-velocity responses to an acute, same-week problem. A standard_experiment scope allows rapid deployment to price-sensitive churn-risk cohorts while measuring both engagement lift and early retention impact before broader commitment.
